1-findings: Kenny said robbery and mistaken identity were possibilities. He said police had found no indication Javits was involved in gang activity. The Daily News reported that Kenny characterized Javits as the embodiment of the American dream. No motive had been publicly announced as of November 13.
2-timeline: Javits’s mother arrived in the United States on November 4. The November 5 vigil came one week after the October 29 shooting; on November 6, the family retained attorney Ben Crump, and the following day’s community walk and candlelight vigil ended near East 171st Street.
3-contradiction: NBC New York, citing law-enforcement sources, said the 17-year-old did not attend DreamYard. Ben Crump said prosecutors told the family they did not believe those responsible went to Javits’s school or were involved in the earlier incident there. Javits’s father had said he believed the shooting was linked to that incident.
4-legal: The 17-year-old faced charges of murder, manslaughter and criminal possession of a weapon, police said. That day, the 17-year-old was arraigned in Bronx Criminal Court before Judge Scott Krompinger and remanded without bail.
5-digital: The Daily News and CBS New York each reported obtaining surveillance video showing Javits running from a person in dark clothing. Kenny said Javits dropped his backpack, which a passerby took; police said it had not been recovered. Kenny said the three returned to collect shell casings, went through Freeman Street station, jumped a turnstile, boarded a southbound No. 5 train and were tracked into Manhattan.
6-turning: Would police make an arrest? On November 11, police announced that a 17-year-old had been arrested and charged with murder.
